text: OLM: past, current and future
EVOLUTION / PLANNED / FUTURE WORK
OLM feature evolution

Past: OLMv0, flawed namespace-local CRD visibility assumptions, SQLite, FBC
Current: OLMv1, ClusterExtension, pins, webhooks
Ongoing: rollouts, config, install, migration
Planned: helm+v2 and v2 schemas. Future: OCI catalog storage.
notes: SLIDE 4: OLM: past, current and futureSPEAKER: OLM A — context / host; name to confirmSTART: 02:45DURATION: 01:15STATUS: EVOLUTION / PLANNED / FUTURE WORKTAKEAWAY: OLM feature evolutionTALK TRACK / SOURCES / CAVEATS / REVIEW:Enumerate the timeline: past work includes OLMv0, SQLite catalogs and established file-based catalogs (FBC). Summarize OLMv0's flawed assumptions about namespace-local CRD visibility, independently managed APIs and watch-aware dependencies. CRD definitions are cluster-scoped shared APIs; custom resource instances may be namespaced, and controller watch scope is configured separately. Shared CRDs can couple operator upgrades. The flawed assumptions belonged to OLMv0's lifecycle model; Kubernetes' cluster-scoped CRD design is the underlying API boundary. Keep the OperatorGroup recap brief and explain how these lessons informed OLMv1. Current OLMv1 capabilities include ClusterExtension, version pins and webhooks. Ongoing development includes resource rollouts, user configuration, direct bundle installation and migration. Direct installation remains an open proposal in PR #2907 at the supplied 2026-10-09 check. Planned work includes Helm content using helm+v2 and v2 catalog schemas. OCI-native catalog storage and transport remain future work. Release-specific availability and feature gates require the source-version qualifications on the detailed slides. The 2025 deck already listed delivered features. A hands off to B after this overview at 04:00. Sources: ../kubecon-2025-slide-context.md slide 9; ../kubecon-2026-resource-assessment.md K-1/K-2/V0-2/V0-3; supplied feature-planning context.SOURCE CONTEXT ROOT: /Users/jordan/Documents/devel/breadcrumbs/2026-kubecon-wip

text: Streamlined Installation

This is in the standard install channel as of <upstreamRelease>

This feature removed the requirement of setting a clusterExtension.spec.serviceAccount (and started ignoring that field if set)

Now, ClusterExtension controller has a cluster-admin SA that it uses for everything, which means CE admins no longer need to find (or create) a service account that has sufficient permissions to manage their installs/updates.

Users should use ValidatingAdmissionPolicy if they want to delegate permission for ClusterExtension management to non-cluster-admins.
Namespace Management

This is in the experimental channel as of release <upstreamRelease>

This feature removed the requirement of setting a clusterExtension.spec.namespace.

Now, the new logic is:- If the namespace is set, we do not manage it. We install bundle objects into it. This is how it has always worked
- If the namespace is not set, we derive a namespace from the bundle itself, potentially with a suggested template or namespace name to use. This enables operator authors to provide namespace metadata (e.g. PSA labels necessary to make the controller pods run). This also makes OLMv1 manage the namespace, just like all of the other bundle objects. That way namespace metadata can be reconciled, etc.

One note: When a ClusterExtension with a managed namespace is deleted, the managed Namespace will be deleted. And that means any unmanaged objects in the namespace will also be deleted.

There's some nuance in the API validations about what kinds of transitions are allowed. (e.g. unset managed namespace to unmanaged namespace might not be allowed)

notes: SLIDE 10: Planned Helm content supportSPEAKER: OLM C — content/catalogs/contributions; name to confirmSTART: 12:00DURATION: 02:00STATUS: PLANNED / helm+v2TAKEAWAY: The rendering contract targets deterministic chart behavior.TALK TRACK / SOURCES / CAVEATS / REVIEW:helm+v2 is the user-confirmed canonical discriminator for versioned OLM Helm packaging/catalog content. Standard chart OCI identity is used, with rendered manifests managed through OLM lifecycle behavior. User values are parsed and validated during rendering. Deterministic rendering is the design goal: features are allow-listed to exclude non-deterministic functionality, with compatibility fixtures required to validate the supported subset. Dependencies are vendored. Hooks and keep behavior are unsupported in the proposal. CRDs use templates/; crds/ is unsupported. Chart release-object mappings and restricted template functions require compatibility testing. Moving CRDs affects upgrade, deletion and data handling. Implementation of proposed gates remains independently unconfirmed. Native chart OCI identity and future OCI catalog storage are separate scopes. Sources: supplied Helm planning brief and feature-planning context.SOURCE CONTEXT ROOT: /Users/jordan/Documents/devel/breadcrumbs/2026-kubecon-wip

notes: SLIDE 11: Catalog performance and content typesSPEAKER: OLM C — content/catalogs/contributions; name to confirmSTART: 14:00DURATION: 01:30STATUS: PLANNED / FUTURE WORKTAKEAWAY: Design for lower catalog-processing cost and additional content types.TALK TRACK / SOURCES / CAVEATS / REVIEW:Credit established FBC capabilities: plaintext editing, composition, extensibility, package-level metadata and version/release properties already exist. The v2 work refines the representation and consumers: less duplicated CSV metadata, version/release fields available directly rather than via property traversal, and explicit mediaType dispatch for installable formats including Helm. Arbitrary FBC schema extensibility alone does not supply end-to-end installation support for a new content type. Catalog processing efficiency is a design benefit to validate, with no measured speedup claimed. Show the practical resolution/metadata work the new representation is intended to reduce. The user-confirmed near-term focus is flexible OLMv1 schemas; OCI-native catalog storage, transport and selective fetching are future work. Channels and legacy graphs are excluded from v2; lifecycle/constraint metadata remains open. Sources: https://olm.operatorframework.io/docs/reference/file-based-catalogs/ ; supplied v2 catalog brief; feature-planning context.SOURCE CONTEXT ROOT: /Users/jordan/Documents/devel/breadcrumbs/2026-kubecon-wip
